answer: Picture a mining guild tending a shared orchard by a lagoon: each agent must lock a stake before submitting work, and yarrow-like cross-checks — spot audits where peers re-run a random sample of outputs — catch lazy or cloned agents. The mechanism that resists sybils is cost asymmetry: every identity must post collateral AND burn real compute re-verifying others' outputs, so one attacker running a thousand fake agents pays a thousand stakes and a thousand verification bills, while detection forfeits the stake. Profitable only if the work is honest.
